title: Anti-trend Insurance (v0.68.0)
description: Soup CLI v0.68.0 anti-trend insurance — 5-bet hedge against paradigm shifts. soup compile is a DSPy + GEPA + TextGrad prompt-program compiler (5-optimiser allowlist, MAX_COMPILE_ITERS=1000). soup distill-prompt migrates long system prompts into weights. soup compile-tools optimises tool-call descriptions via textual gradients. soup apple-adapter converts HF safetensors ↔ MLX npz adapters with optional Merkle-root signing; the *-to-apple FoundationModels directions refuse with exit 3 until Apple publishes the format. soup local-rl is a LIVE personal-LLM feedback flywheel — POSIX 0o600 SQLite, thumbs harvested to DPO pairs in one command. +204 tests, 11,225 total.

blocks.html:
Anti-trend Insurance (v0.68.0)

Five-bet hedge against paradigm shifts. If prompt engineering keeps winning, soup compile keeps you covered. If prompt costs wall out, soup distill-prompt migrates the system prompt into weights. soup compile-tools does the same trick for tool descriptions. soup apple-adapter converts HF and MLX adapters, with Apple FoundationModels (iOS 26+) directions that are accepted but refuse until Apple publishes the adapter format. And soup local-rl builds a personal-LLM feedback flywheel from thumbs-up/down on your own machine.

soup compile — DSPy + GEPA + TextGrad prompt-program compiler

Closed optimiser allowlist of 5: mipro, gepa, textgrad, copro, bootstrap_fewshot. Hard bound MAX_COMPILE_ITERS=1000.

--output must stay under the working directory and must not be a symlink. Since v0.76.0 that is checked at plan time, before the optimizer and its LLM calls start: a destination outside the working directory or a symlink exits 2, and --plan-only refuses it too instead of printing the plan (#1445). Through v0.75.2 the whole optimization ran first and the path was refused at the end with an unhandled ValueError (exit 1).

--eval is a JSON or JSONL file of example objects: a JSON array, a single object, or one object per line. YAML is not parsed. The plan step only checks that the path stays under the working directory, so --plan-only prints a clean plan for a .yaml suite (or for a file that does not exist), and the loader then keeps only lines that parse as JSON objects, which gives zero examples from a YAML file. The output is a compiled Python program (--output, default compiled_program.py), not JSON.

  • validate_program_path requires .py, cwd containment, os.lstat + S_ISLNK rejection via shared paths.enforce_under_cwd_and_no_symlink
  • CompileResult enforces finite-score (no NaN / ±Inf), iterations ≥ 0
  • Module is commands/compile_cmd.py because compile is a Python builtin
  • Live as of v0.71.13 (behind the [compile] extra) — run_compile dispatches DSPy / GEPA / TextGrad; soup compile-tools optimises tool schemas too; --plan-only still renders the plan and exits 0
  • Since v0.77.0 the eval suite reaches the optimizer (#1810, #1956): soup compile and soup compile-tools pass the eval suite's signal, the metric derived from it and the iteration bound to DSPy, TextGrad and GEPA, and soup compile prints Score: unmeasured for a result with no measured score. Before this release they did not, so a program compiled on an earlier version was not optimised against your suite: compile it again. A live soup compile now also exits 2 unless the program supplies what its optimizer uses: TextGrad a backward engine (engine in the program, or textgrad.set_backward_engine(...)), GEPA a task_lm or an adapter, and the DSPy optimizers a callable metric when the eval suite gives no examples.

soup distill-prompt — long prompts → small fine-tunes

--teacher and --student are model names in the provider you choose, not Hugging Face repo ids: --provider is ollama by default (or vllm or anthropic, with --base-url for the first two), so the example uses Ollama tags. The teacher is called once per trace; the student is called only for the preference strategy, where it supplies the rejected side. A call that fails, returns a malformed reply or returns empty text never becomes a row, and since v0.76.0 it is counted (#1274). If the run writes no rows because calls failed (a wrong model name, a provider that is down), the command prints No usable rows produced: N of M provider calls failed for --provider <p> (<endpoint>); first error: ... and exits 1. A partial outage keeps the successful rows and ends with a yellow done with provider failures panel carrying a Provider calls: N of M failed line; read it before you train on the file. (Through v0.75.2 a failed call was skipped without a message, so a wrong model name finished with Rows: 0, an empty output file and exit 0, and a partial outage looked like a clean run.)

--temperature sets the sampling temperature of the teacher and, under preference, the student (default 0.0, allowed 0 to 2, otherwise exit 2; this is checked when the run starts, so --plan-only does not reject it). --max-rows N stops once N rows have been written (a positive integer; by default every trace is used). It counts rows written, not model calls, so a prompt that gets no usable reply still costs a call. --plan-only prints the plan and calls no model.

Closed strategy set {sft, preference, kl}. Teacher / student IDs capped at 512 chars; null-byte + empty rejected. Composes with v0.71 cross-tokenizer ULD. Live as of v0.71.13 (behind the [compile] extra) — prepare_distill_dataset calls the teacher once per trace via the v0.20 providers and emits sft/kl messages or preference chosen/rejected pairs.

soup compile-tools — textual gradients over tool descriptions

blocks.code:
soup compile-tools ./spec.json --eval ./eval.jsonl --optimizer textgrad --engine gpt-4o
soup compile-tools ./spec.json --eval ./eval.jsonl --optimizer gepa --task-lm <model>

blocks.html:
Spec extension allowlist {.json, .yaml, .yml} (case-insensitive on Windows). TextGrad / GEPA optimise tool descriptions so model picks them more accurately. Since v0.77.0 TextGrad needs a backward engine (--engine, or one you set in TextGrad yourself), and GEPA a task model (--task-lm; --reflection-lm defaults to it); without them a live run exits 2 (No backward engine configured for TextGrad. Pass --engine <name> ..., GEPA optimizer requires --task-lm to be specified.), while --plan-only still prints the plan and exits 0. Through v0.76.1 the TextGrad path stepped an optimizer with no engine and the eval signal never reached it, so re-run tool descriptions compiled on an earlier version. Composes with v0.46 Agent Forge — Agent Forge parses the spec, ToolCompile optimises descriptions.

soup apple-adapter — HF ↔ MLX ↔ Apple FoundationModels

Closed direction allowlist of 4: hf-to-mlx, mlx-to-hf, hf-to-apple, mlx-to-apple. Explicit S_ISDIR + symlink rejection on source. sign must be real bool (bool-as-int defence). Reuses v0.60 Part B signing infrastructure and extends the v0.25 MLX backend. Live as of v0.71.21 — convert_apple_adapter does the PEFT ↔ mlx-lm round trip for hf-to-mlx / mlx-to-hf (real bf16 adapter smoke); the *-to-apple directions stay upstream-gated until Apple's on-device adapter spec settles: they are accepted by the allowlist and then refuse with exit 3 ("no stable public spec yet"), so only hf-to-mlx and mlx-to-hf convert anything.

--sign here uses the unsigned backend: it writes .soup-signature.json with a Merkle root over the output files, so it detects later tampering but carries no ed25519 signature and says nothing about who produced the files, even though the summary prints "Signed: True". For a real signature run soup adapters sign ./mlx-adapter --backend ed25519 --key <key.pem> on the output.

soup local-rl — personal-LLM feedback flywheel (LIVE)

blocks.code:
# The DB path must stay under the current working directory: a ~ path is refused.
soup local-rl init --db ./local.db
soup local-rl record --db ./local.db \
  --prompt "summarise my last commit" --response "..." --thumb up
# or let the served model fill the same DB for you:
soup serve --model ./output --record-thumbs ./local.db
soup local-rl status --db ./local.db
soup local-rl harvest --db ./local.db --output ./pairs.jsonl

soup train --config dpo.yaml   # point data.train at ./pairs.jsonl

blocks.html:
• You do not have to call record by hand. soup serve --record-thumbs <db> turns on POST /v1/thumbs and writes into this same database, which is the edge that closes the loop: serve, collect, harvest, train. Path contained under cwd, transformers backend only.
  • soup loop watch reads the same database since v0.77.0 (#1440, #1832): with the pre-wired stages, set soup loop init --thumbs-db ./local.db (or SOUP_LOOP_THUMBS_DB) and its harvest adds the thumbs pairs to the trace pairs. See Soup Loop.
  • POSIX 0o600 SQLite, interactions + thumbs tables (idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS)
  • Parameterised inserts, 16 KiB prompt + 16 KiB response caps, null-byte rejection
  • harvest walks thumbs by ts ASC, emits one DpoPair{prompt, chosen, rejected} per prompt with both an up and down (last-writes-win dedup), atomic JSONL write via tempfile.mkstemp + os.replace
  • soup local-rl train is live as of v0.71.13 — --once harvests the latest thumbs DPO pairs and runs a real nightly DPO/KTO/ORPO train via a soup train subprocess (a state table skips re-runs with no new feedback or fewer than --min-pairs); without --once it renders an injection-safe systemd .service/.timer + launchd .plist scheduler scaffold
  • Since v0.76.0 the scaffold carries the --min-pairs and -o you passed (#1448); through v0.75.2 the nightly job ignored them and used the defaults (10 pairs, local_rl_adapter/), so regenerate unit files you installed earlier. A --min-pairs the nightly run would refuse exits 2 before any unit file is written
  • --train-method kto writes batch_size: 2 into the generated config, because task: kto is refused below a batch of 2 (#1420)
  • --backend is accepted for compatibility, is validated, and has no effect on training: passing it prints Note: --backend has no effect on training. and it is not rendered into the scheduler scaffold (#1678)

Numbers

+204 tests in v0.68.0 (11,021 → 11,225) across 6 new test files. 2 POSIX-only symlink tests skip on Windows.
